title: It's really sunny now!
vocab_topic: Good weather and bad weather; Free-time activities
pair_game: Act out a word with no talking. Your partner guesses it. Then swap!

grammar_box.title: Let’s / Let’s not
grammar_box.tip: Let’s = Let us. Let’s + verb: Let’s swim! (Keling, …)

questions: What is the weather like in your city today? Do you like it?
What do you like to do on a sunny day?
What do you do on rainy days when you can't go outside?
What is your favorite free-time activity? Do you do it alone or with friends?
What activities do you suggest to your friends when the weather is good?
What is the worst weather you have ever experienced?
Do you prefer hot or cold weather? Why?
What do you usually do after school to relax?
Describe the seasons in your city — which one is the best?
What free-time activity would you like to try but never have?
starters: Today it’s … in … . I like / don’t like it.
On rainy days I … at home.
My favourite activity is … . I do it with … .
The worst weather was … . It was very … .
In … it’s … . The best season is … .
samples: What do you like to do on a sunny day?
On a **sunny** day I **ride my bike** in the park. Sometimes I **swim**.
What activities do you suggest to your friends when the weather is good?
I say, “**Let’s play** football!” or “**Let’s go** to the park!”
Do you prefer hot or cold weather? Why?
I like **cold** weather. I love snow! In summer Tashkent is very **hot**.

survey.title: Class survey
survey.question: What do you do on a rainy day?

game.title: Weather dice
game.rules: Roll the dice. Read the weather. Say “Let’s …!” Your partner says “Good idea!” or “Let’s not!”

mini_talk.title: A fun weekend plan
plan: Say what you like to do
mini_talk.model: Hi, Ali! It’s **really sunny** today. It’s warm, too. I don’t want to watch TV. **Let’s go** to the park! **Let’s play** football and ride our bikes. **Let’s not** stay at home. After that, **let’s eat** ice cream. See you at four!

cando: make plans with Let’s and Let’s not
